headline: Majors hold the 200-day line while momentum overbought; whales moving coins onto exchanges as stablecoin float tightens.
paragraphs: The regime is above the 200-day simple moving average across all seven majors tracked, but the picture splits cleanly on trend confirmation. Bitcoin, Solana, and XRP show MACD above signal line, suggesting uptrend momentum remains intact, while Ethereum, BNB, Doge, and ADA show MACD below signal, indicating that technical momentum has already begun to diverge from price. Ethereum alone has completed a golden cross (price above the 50-day above the 200-day), a rare structural alignment; the others sit above the 200-day but have not yet reclaimed the 50-day hurdle. The regime is not fragile, it is not below the long-term line, but it is not accelerating either. The market is in a pause state, not a breakdown.

Momentum readings across the board have pushed into the overbought zone. Bitcoin RSI sits at 67.7, Ethereum at 67.3, Solana at 67.1, and even the weaker performers like XRP (62.0) and BNB (63.5) are trending toward the 70 threshold where reversals become statistically common. The Fear and Greed gauge has climbed to 69 (Greed territory) after ranging between 25 and 74 over the last month, meaning the crowd has moved from panic lows into euphoria in a single window. This is the textbook divergence: momentum indicators stretched, but the underlying trend (MACD split, no golden crosses except Ethereum) is not uniformly confirming. When RSI gets this crowded and MACD starts to roll over, the tape is suggesting fatigue rather than fresh conviction.

Derivatives positioning shows heavy longs across all majors. Bitcoin's long-to-short ratio stands at 1.23 with funding running at 0.66% per 8 hours (7.2% annualized), Ethereum at 1.26 with funding at 6.5%, and XRP at 2.45 with the highest absolute funding at 11.0% per annum. This structure means traders are paying significantly to hold leveraged long exposure, and in Bitcoin's case the past four hours saw 100 liquidations with shorts getting crushed (shorts liquidated: $8,195 versus longs: $856,346). The anomaly is Solana, where funding has flipped negative at minus 0.87% per 8 hours (minus 9.6% annualized), a sign that shorts are now paying to hold their bets because the crowd has become so tilted long. Open interest remains elevated across the board (Bitcoin at $2.2 billion, Ethereum at $1.6 billion), which means there is substantial capital in the boat but also fragility if one domino moves.

Whale and institutional flows are the data point most worth watching. Over the past 24 hours, $126 million net moved onto exchanges, driven almost entirely by Ethereum ($109 million onto Coinbase Institutional) and Bitcoin inflows to Coinbase and Coinbase Institutional. Simultaneously, $154 million in USDC moved off exchanges from Coinbase Institutional, a near-equivalent swap of stablecoins for spot exposure. Over the broader window, the weekly trend has been consistent accumulation onto exchanges: week ending August 11 saw $493 million move onto exchanges, August 18 another $489 million, August 25 saw a spike to $1,040 million, and the nascent week ending September 1 already shows $226 million. This is not position-taking for a rip higher; this is supply staging. The stablecoin float sits at $309 billion, up 1.18% over the month, so dry powder has expanded modestly.

On the day, prices across the majors have drifted lower: Bitcoin down 0.8%, Ethereum down 0.6%, Solana down 0.8%. On the week, the picture inverts, Bitcoin up 1.1%, Ethereum up 1.2%, Solana up 8.8%, a pattern replicated in a muted form across most names. Over the month, all seven are positive, ranging from Doge at 14.8% to Solana at 31.4%. The daily weakness into overbought momentum and rising institutional supply onto exchanges (not off) reads as early profit-taking or position adjustment, not capitulation. Total market cap is down 2.81% on the day to $2.64 trillion, with Bitcoin dominance steady at 59.1%. ETF flows remain supportive: Bitcoin saw $216.7 million inflow on August 31 and $803.6 million net over the last five sessions, while Ethereum posted $87.6 million on the day and $787.7 million over five sessions with ten consecutive same-direction days, a persistence that flags institutional demand as structural rather than opportunistic.

Watch for the next pivot. If Bitcoin and Ethereum reclaim their 50-day moving averages (a golden cross would confirm), momentum could re-accelerate. If, instead, the daily weakness persists while the weekly and monthly trends flatten, the overbought RSI and negative MACD divergence in most names could translate into a multi-week consolidation. The whale flow reversal would be the hard tell: if Ethereum and Bitcoin begin moving off exchanges rather than onto them, conviction has shifted. For now, the tape shows strong hands staging supply while the crowd feels greedy and technicals are exhausted at the top of a three-month uptrend. That is a condition, not a direction.
